S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with an initial account of known impacts and response actions. Affected customers must be notified within 24 hours when an incident presents an ongoing or serious safety risk, and otherwise within 5 business days.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with an initial account of known impacts and response actions. A complete report, including investigation findings and any corrective measures, is due within 30 days; material new findings must be provided promptly. Affected customers must be notified within 24 hours when an incident presents an ongoing or serious safety risk, and otherwise within 5 business days. Reports must identify the model and installed-unit population and may not omit incidents because their cause is still under investigation.

parameters.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and adequate representative sampling. Manufacturers shall provide per-model test results, including failure rates, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy that model, and retain results for audit. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate must submit a corrective-action plan and be retested within 12 months. Regulators may require interim safeguards based on results; exceeding the threshold alone does not automatically require a market ban.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and adequate representative sampling. Manufacturers shall provide per-model test results, including failure rates, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy that model, and retain results for audit. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate must submit a corrective-action plan and be retested within 12 months. Regulators may require interim safeguards based on results; exceeding the threshold alone does not automatically require a market ban.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and adequate representative sampling. Manufacturers shall provide per-model test results, including failure rates, to the relevant regulator and to customers who buy that model, and retain results for audit. A model exceeding a 5% failure rate must submit a corrective-action plan and be retested within 12 months. Regulators may require interim safeguards based on results; exceeding the threshold alone does not automatically require a market ban.

parameters.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when a serious hazard is identified and provide updates as investigations or remedies progress.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when a serious hazard is identified and provide updates as investigations or remedies progress.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Customers shall receive clear safety notices describing relevant hazards, affected models or serial ranges, immediate precautions, and how to obtain support. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when a serious hazard is identified and provide updates as investigations or remedies progress. A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Calculate the rate by model and calendar year, using the model’s average number of installed units during that year as the denominator and the number of distinct thermal incidents involving that model as the numerator. Count incidents regardless of whether investigation is complete; incidents provisionally attributed to a model shall be included and updated if later findings change the attribution. Manufacturers shall document the calculation and supporting records for regulator verification. When the trigger is met, the manufacturer shall promptly notify regulators and affected customers, stop distribution of the affected model, and provide a regulator-approved remedy, including repair, replacement, or refund.

judge_section_notes: S1 is strict (all incidents reported within 24 hours, even while cause is under investigation, with 24-hour customer notice for serious risk), and S5 keeps the firm 8/100,000 mandatory recall with no phase-in, no corrective-action substitute and only 'promptly' notices - so Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) is caught while Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.4) is not. S2 keeps the 55 °C / 5% test and gives numeric failure rates to buyers and regulators but not the public, yet an above-limit model is only required to submit a corrective-action plan and retest within 12 months, with no automatic ban or sales stop. S3 and S4 sit inside the acceptable ranges (24-month new-unit shut-off with a 6-year retrofit floor and interim instructions; built-in suppression at 36 months with a regulator-approved equivalent).
